newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mostly down on softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mostly down on softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended lower Monday in a moderate session, undermined by light profit taking amid reports of slightly softer cash prices, industry sources said.
May slipped 1.7 cents to close at $2.064 per million British thermal units. June settled 1.1 cents lower at $2.131. Others ended mixed, with 1999s up slightly.

"We've got a double top (at $2.09 in May) and a double bottom (at $2.035, and we're stuck in the middle, but cash was weaker this morning and people started taking some profits," said one Midwest trader.

While most traders expected a pullback after last week's sharp gains amid record open interest, there was little conviction about market direction. Spreads still favor early injections, but storage is comfortable and milder spring weather is likely to arrive soon, they said.

Chart traders pegged near-support in May at $2.035, with further buying likely at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825. Key resistance was seen at $2.095, the intraday high from March 10, with a break above that level probably triggering a move to the $2.16 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to down slightly at about $2.05. Midcontinent pipes showed similar movement to the low-to-mid $1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate fell by about five cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 1.5 cents to $2.226. NYMEX said 48,040 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 48,736.
NYMEX May natgas goes off the board Thursday, April 24.

On the KCBT, May finished 2.2 cents lower at $1.93, while deferreds ended down by one-half cent. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 13.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 55 lots changed hands, down sharply from Friday's total of 244.
KCBT May natgas expires Friday, April 25.
